3/26/26 3:00PM Update:
Good afternoon Shredders!  Sun is out vibes are high and the groomers are riding phenomenally today.  What started as a clear and crisp day ended up more spring feeling with temps in the mid thirties. The weather is looking pretty similar tomorrow so bring some sunscreen, sunglasses and your best spring outfit. Join us for another marvelous day at Crystal Mountain! 

Kelly's gap, Northway, Lower Ferks, Deerfly, Exterminator are closed the season. Please do not duck the ropes they are there for a reason.

Terrain Parks: Discovery Park, Sudden Drop and Arwine's Jump Line are all open today! 

Events:
  • Intro to Backcountry Touring: Offered Daily March 27th, 28th, and 29th, learn the essentials of backcountry travel in a beginner-friendly setting in this three-hour clinic. 
  • Nachtspektakel: On March 28th from 4-9PM tour under the stars indulge in tasty food & drink, hang out around the fire, and revel with other like-minded individuals. Then slide down the mountain in complete darkness, guided only by the stars and your headlamp!
  • Avalanche Awareness Night: On March 27th from 4-6pm the experts from the Northwest Avalanche Center will guide us through the curriculum while relating information specific to the Crystal Mountain area. This free class provides a basic approach to managing risk in winter sports.
  • Junior Ski Patrol: On March 29th, young girls will learn mountain safety and first aid while working with the strong members of the ski patrol community. This event is intended for intermediate to expert skiers/snowboarders ages 8 - 17 who identify as female.
Notes for today:
  1. $199 Spring 3-Day Passes are on sale now! Ski for just $67 a day, any day of the week, for the rest of the season! 
  2. This coming weekend, March 28th-29th will be the last weekend Parking Reservations are required. 
  3. The Crystal Express Shuttle service will end this weekend 3/29. 
  4. Looking to save time and make the most of the day? Consider grabbing a Daily Reserve Upgrade! Available on weekends and holidays, this upgrade grants access to priority lift access, getting you on the lift quicker and fresh tracks faster. 
  5. Don't forget to check out Crystal Mountain Outfitters for their Spring Sale going on right now! Save up to 50% on all 25-26 winter items. (Some exclusions may apply)
  6. Swing by Brand X and check out all this year's demos for sale at a great price!
  7. Did you know it just takes 5 Days to be entered to win a 26/27 Ikon Pass? Track your days on the Ikon App and register for RIDE TO WIN
  8. Paid reservations can only be cancelled by emailing SP+ at  CrystalMtnParking@spplus.com with Reservation #, First Name, and Last Name. While you may not receive an immediate reply, the cancellation will be processed. The Crystal Mountain Contact Center cannot process these cancellations.
  9. Parking refunds for guests who paid for parking reservations March 14 & 15 are expected to be completed through SP+ by March 31st. No email is necessary.  
  10. In case of on-mountain emergency: Call 360-663-3064 or 911

Mountain Weather 3/26/2026 4:20pm 

Forecaster: Chris Pleasance

Synopsis: Throw on your spring fit—it's time to harvest some corn. Mild air is seeping into the region as a weak upper-level ridge nestles over the Cascades, strengthening through this evening. A calm, clear night will deliver a solid overnight freeze, setting the stage for a classic diurnal cycle on Friday. The morning starts chilly, but that powerful March sun will start putting in work the moment it hits the slopes. With light winds offering little cooling relief, expect corn o’clock before noon! Fortunately, temps look to stay reasonable enough to keep the snow from getting too sloppy, making Friday a prime day for spring laps.

12hr Precip: None

Extended: Saturday looks to be the nicest day of the weekend with the last bit of our ridge hanging on before a new trough sags southward into the PNW. Temps won’t be quite as warm on Saturday, but mostly sunny skies and light winds should still make for soft spring turns. Sunday starts to flip the script as we welcome a weak low pressure system into our region. This pattern change should provide lower freezing levels and a couple inches of snow, if we’re lucky. 

*Daily Summaries: 12hr period representing 4am-4pm or 4pm-4am data
*Freezing Elevation (ft): Approximate elevation above sea level where the air temperature reaches 32 degree F
